concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of blurred vision and sudden vision loss, combined with the imaging findings of focal enhancement along the enlarged right optic nerve and the pathological examination showing a hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm, support the diagnosis of a glioma of the optic nerve.

The patient's sudden vision loss and the imaging findings of occlusion of the superior branch artery and combined occlusion of the central retinal artery and vein support the diagnosis of a central retinal artery occlusion.
The patient's symptoms of blurred vision and the imaging findings of mild and marked swelling of the optic disc support the diagnosis of optic disc swelling.

The patient's symptoms of sudden vision loss and the imaging findings of peripapillary retinal hemorrhages and occlusion of the superior branch artery support the diagnosis of a retinal vascular occlusion.

rationales.F01: Blurred vision in one eye could indicate optic nerve involvement, suggesting glioma of the optic nerve.
rationales.F02: Sudden vision loss is consistent with central retinal artery occlusion or optic nerve glioma.
rationales.F05: Mild swelling of the optic disc is a common finding in optic disc swelling.
rationales.F07: Marked swelling of the optic disc is a strong indicator of optic disc swelling.
rationales.F09: Occlusion of the superior branch artery is a characteristic finding in central retinal artery occlusion and retinal vascular occlusion.
rationales.F10: Focal enhancement along the enlarged optic nerve is highly suggestive of glioma of the optic nerve.
rationales.F11: Hypercellular sample with astrocytic neoplasm is diagnostic of glioma of the optic nerve.
rationales.F12: Positive immunohistochemistry results for glial fibrillary acid protein, oligodendrocyte transcription factor 2, mutant IDH-1 protein, and p53 are characteristic of glioma of the optic nerve.
